United States Department of the Interior
OFFICE OF THE SECRETARY

NORTHEAST REGION

JOHN F. KENNEDY FEDERAL BUILDING

ROOM 2003 J & K

BOSTON, MASSACHUSETTS 02203
ER 75/1018
December 1, 1975
Mr. David Strohm
Director
Office of Community Development
City of Boston
Office of the Mayor
City Hall, Room 703
Boston, Massachusetts
Dear Mr. Strohm:
This responds to a request for our Department's review and commentary on the draft environmental statement for proposed Clearance of Unsafe Buildings Community Development Block Grant Program in Boston, Massachusetts.
In general, we find this a well done environmental statement. Pages 21 and 22 describe the CDBC Revival program of using vacant lots for gardening and open space purposes. This is a commendable program and we encourage its application to the presently proposed action.
The recitation of the Advisory Council on Historic Preservation procedures (Section V and Appendix D), the extensive listing of historic sites (Section V and Appendices E and F) and reference to contacts and consultation with the State Historic Preservation Officer and Boston Landmarks Commission demonstrate an understanding of the needs and requirements for cultural resource protection. The commitment on page 126 that the City of Boston, as a measure to mitigate harm, will comply with "... 106... procedures ... outlined in Appendix D" is assurance of affirmative action to be taken when this proposal can be focused on specific structural demolition projects.
While in general above-ground nature of unsafe building clearance would not appear to affect subsurface cultural resources such as archeological data, there is the possibility on some work sites that such archeological values may be disturbed. This matter should be addressed, at least in a potential or probability sense, in this environmental statement, as evaluation of archeological resource findings could entail follow through of the procedures mentioned above. In handling this matter,
